BANK_P3X.title: Stuck? Hail Mary
BANK_P3X.promo: Stuck on one? Hail Mary: 4 moves for a smart guess.
BANK_P3X.intro: You lose nothing for a wrong bubble, so you fill in every one. Here is how to make the guess a good one.

cards.b: Round every number to one digit. Use g = 10. Work in powers of ten. Cross off any choice more than about 1.5 times away from your estimate. Example: the sun puts out about 4e26 W. For 1 microsecond that is 4e20 J, about 1e14 kWh, about 1e13 dollars. Cross off every choice far from 10 trillion. In 42 of 60 practice questions, you could cross off 2 or more choices this way.

Skip a number copied straight from the question. It was a wrong choice in 3 of 20 Exam 1 questions. With two-number vector choices, work out the direction. The choices often differ only by sign or order. Ignore middle, biggest, smallest, double and odd-one-out. Each scored about 20%, the same as a blind pick.

Count the letters of the answers you trust. Pick the letter you used least. In the practice exams each letter was the key 3 to 5 times out of 20. One stuck question: about 45% if the rest are right. Three stuck: about 40%. If you doubt the rest: near 20%.
A wrong bubble costs you nothing. Save 2 minutes at the end and fill every one.

BANK_P3X.odds: Honest odds: a blind guess is 20%. Estimate plus cross-off is about 50% on questions you can set up. The least-used letter is about 40 to 45% when the rest is right. Practice exams are not the real exam.

constants.title: Constants for this exam
constants.intro: Look them up on your calculator instead of typing digits from memory. Exam 3 uses these.

casio: Your Casio cover often has the constant list printed inside. Check it before the exam.
Worst case: press SHIFT 7, then try numbers until the symbol you need shows up. There are only 40.
